title: Effects of interactive video-based abdominal ultrasound e-learning on diagnostic competence of medical students: a prospective, single-centre, randomised controlled trial
summary:
Background
Ultrasound is one of the most common diagnostic procedures in medicine. Proficiency in ultrasound consists of two core competencies: image acquisition and image interpretation. To date, this skill has often been practiced only in a limited and unstructured manner during medical school. A digital learning program could help: it would allow students to practice evaluating what they see using videos of real ultrasound examinations. The videos do not show any names or other identifying information about the person being examined. Whether video-based e-learning actually improves this skill has hardly been studied to date.

Research Question
We want to determine whether medical students’ ability to correctly interpret ultrasound images changes as a result of practicing with a digital learning program featuring ultrasound videos.

Methodology
Medical students at Witten/Herdecke University in their 5th semester are eligible to participate. Participation is voluntary. Participants are randomly assigned to two groups. One group practices using the digital learning program over five days. The other group learns through the university’s traditional introductory course on the abdominal ultrasound. Before and after the practice phase, all participants take a test. In the test, they view ultrasound videos and assess whether they are normal or abnormal and where in the ultrasound image they suspect the abnormality is located. The program and peer tutors evaluate these answers according to set criteria. Peer tutors do not know which group a participant belongs to. In addition, participants complete a questionnaire regarding their assessment of their own skills and the learning program. All data is analyzed anonymously.
conditions: Medical education: ultrasound reporting competence in medical students (healthy volunteers)

interventions.name:
Intervention Group (Group A)
In addition to the regular basic abdominal ultrasound course (3 course days + 1 exam day), participants gain access to the interactive online video training (“Interpretation-Trainer”) via the university’s internal learning platform, Moodle, immediately after the prelimi

Waiting Control Group (Group B)
Participants take part exclusively in the regular basic abdominal ultrasound course (3 course days + 1 exam day), without access to the interpretation trainer. Access to the identical interpretation trainer is granted the day after the final exam.

Data collection

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Enrollment in the medical program at Witten/Herdecke University
Completion of the introductory abdominal ultrasound course in the 5th semester (currently, as a make-up session, or in the past) or another equivalent ultrasound course
Voluntary consent to participate
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of consent
Incomplete participation in the Sono Basic Course on the Abdomen or an equivalent ultrasound course
Serving as an ultrasound tutor for the Sono AG at UW/H
Participation as a test subject in a beta version of the Findings Trainer
